Hi Olga —

Thanks for the recap. We started a quick smoke integration yesterday and hit intermittent 502s when calling the embeddings endpoint and subsequently the reranker. High-level notes:

- Occurrence: 502s ~2–3x per 1000 requests during batch ingestion (embeddings then reranker call).
- Timing: roughly 09:32–09:50 PST yesterday (we captured a few traces).
- Impact: the ingestion job retries but it’s slowing throughput; we also saw a malformed JSON error in our gateway logs.

I attached finexus-502-trace.log and a sample-payload.json (sanitized). The payload contains our preprocessor output — an array of embeddings objects. We are using the Redwood JS SDK (installer via npm) with default timeout (30s).

Questions: could KV cache interaction or structured output/tool-calling cause a gateway 502?

Thanks —
Sam

Hi Sam —

Appreciate the quick artifacts. First-pass observations and asks:

1) Please confirm the exact Redwood SDK version (npm ls @redwood/inference or package.json) — older SDKs serialized arrays slightly differently which can trip our gateway validation.
2) Can you paste the full request headers (Authorization, Content-Type) for one failing request? Content-Type mismatches (application/json vs application/json; charset=utf-8) have surfaced in the past.
3) Try a direct curl to the hosted endpoint (we’ve included a repro-template in my CC) with the sample-payload.json and run with --trace or --verbose so we can see HTTP-level details.
4) For short-term verification, increase client timeout to 60s and disable automatic SDK retries to prevent duplicate inflight requests.

Possible vectors: payload serialization (array of embeddings objects), unexpected Content-Length from streaming preprocessor, or gateway validation rejecting nested tool-calling metadata. KV cache on its own shouldn’t throw 502s — it typically causes stale responses or misses.

If you can paste the curl and headers I’ll try to reproduce locally on staging and we’ll post an initial hypothesis. I’ve attached a quick repro-template for your convenience.

—Aditya

Thanks — confirming details below and pasting a minimal repro curl:

- SDK: @redwood/inference@0.9.1 (installed via npm)
- Headers: Authorization: Bearer REDACTED, Content-Type: application/json
- Observed failure: gateway returned HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway with body "invalid request payload" for 3 different batches.

Minimal curl (sanitized):

curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/batch \
  -d @sample-payload.json --verbose

sample-payload.json is attached (the embedding array is under payload.documents[].embeddings). We also include a small structured metadata object per document used by our reranker pipeline — that might be the odd field.

We will run the curl with --trace and paste headers; attaching sample-payload.json now. Also, we observed the 502 even when we called the endpoint directly (outside our gateway) so my suspicion is gateway validation on Redwood side but worth investigating KV/structured metadata.

—Kira

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Kira Tanaka <kira.t@finexus.com>, Sam Carter <sam.carter@finexus.com>
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-27T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick recap + integration next steps

Thanks for the repro and traces — we reproduced the 502 on staging with your sample payload. Summary of what we found and plan:

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed in staging): our gateway validation rejects requests where the JSON body contains an embeddings array nested under a non-standard path (payload.documents[].embeddings) combined with an extra metadata object named "tools". The gateway JSON schema expects embeddings under top-level "embeddings" or a recognized "documents" structure; when it encounters the nested array plus unrecognized "tools" object it returns a 502 during the validation step rather than a 4xx. This is an unfortunate failure mode and we’ll patch the validator to return a 400 with a clear error message.

Immediate mitigation (short term):
- We will add a routing fallback so that if validation fails we send the payload to a permissive ingestion path and log the exact schema mismatch. This reduces customer impact while we ship a proper validation fix. ETA: 48 hours for the fallback rule.

Medium-term fix:
- Patch gateway validator to accept the nested documents.embeddings shape or return detailed 400 errors.
- Add a diagnostic flag to the SDK that will normalize payloads for customers using preprocessor outputs (we’ll propose an SDK patch v0.9.2). ETA: next week for SDK patch + validator changes in staging, two weeks for production rollout.

Action items:
1) Olga/Marissa to enable fallback route for Finexus (Ops) — target: +48h.
2) Aditya to prepare validator PR and SDK normalization change — target: next-week staging test.
3) Finexus: small change to preprocessor to push embeddings to top-level embeddings array or enable SDK normalization once v0.9.2 is available.

I created a Jira ticket INF-7321 (linked below) and copied a short set of debug notes. We’ll update the ticket with logs and the staging repro.

Thanks again for the fast turnaround — I’ll coordinate timelines and ping for a 30-min follow-up once we have the fallback live.

—Connor
